items.title: John Beal interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 18, 2024
items.q: Tony Bennett was one of the artists on the show and he wanted to do “I Left My Heart in San Francisco” and Duke was not that familiar with that tune, and he would wait for my bass note

ctx.x: It seems to me that bassists have a burden to carry that other — especially horn players — don’t, and that is someone calls a tune and you are the foundation. You’re the harmonic foundation and the time, and if you don’t know the tune who are you going to depend on to get through it? So how do you learn tunes, how did you learn the standards so that you were as prepared as possible?

Well I started out listening, playing along with records like one of the first records I played with was Erroll Garner, who had a great beat, right? And you could find the bass notes pretty easily. So your ear gets attuned through fitting in what’s going on, and you depend — a lot of times you’ll depend on a piano player, but a lot of times the piano player depends on you. I had to play with Duke Ellington’s band one time and it was a TV show. And I remember Joe Benjamin had a fender bender and I was on the beach…
In like one beat, right? You latch on within a beat?
